subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex performance targets
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex performance targets

Hi Alice

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the immediate asks we discussed so we can get a sizing estimate over the next 48 hours: 

1) Target SLOs and primary use cases
   - Latency SLOs: p50/p95 targets for prompt lengths under 256 tokens (you mentioned <200ms p50, ~400ms p95 as a goal) confirm?
   - Streaming: you said streaming for multi-turn assistant sessions is required (live token streaming to the client)

2) Workload profile we need to size:
   - Avg tokens per request (prompt + expected completion)
   - Avg QPS during steady-state and peak QPS (15m peak window)
   - Peak concurrent requests (how many simultaneous sessions will be active)
   - Typical session length (requests per session) and burst patterns (cron/ETL vs human-driven)

3) Model and perf constraints
   - Target model family (open Llama3-70B quantized? or smaller/faster variant)
   - Any mandatory quantization or strict privacy constraints (customer-managed KMS)

Attachments: I can share a small CSV template to collect these numbers if useful attaching a one-line template and we can drop your answers into it.

Next step: If you can reply with the numbers above (avg tokens per request, steady vs peak QPS, concurrency, whether streaming is required for all traffic), Marissa will put together a sizing and cost estimate and propose a dedicated vs shared configuration. If you'd prefer, we can set a 30-min sizing call tomorrow.

Thanks
Rafael
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood_throughput_template.csv (1 KB, CSV stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@finex.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 12:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex performance targets

Hi Alice

Following Rafael's note, a few concrete data points that help us produce a tight throughput sizing (I put these into the attached CSV template):

- Workload basics we need (please fill if possible):
  * avg_tokens_per_request: tokens for typical prompt + expected completion (e.g., 120 prompt + 60 completion = 180)
  * requests_per_second_steady: typical QPS outside peaks
  * requests_per_second_peak: 15-minute peak QPS you expect
  * avg_concurrency: number of simultaneous open sessions sending requests (approx)
  * session_length_requests: average RPCs per user session
  * streaming_required: yes/no (do you need server->client token streaming for the UX?)
  * desired_latency_slos: p50/p95 targets in ms for responses <256 tokens

- Additional perf/quality details:
  * do you rely on long context (>= 8k tokens) or mostly short contexts?
  * any KV prefix caching opportunities (reused system prompts, short-term convo cache)?
  * tail-latency sensitivity (is p99 important for your UX?)

Quick example (so you see how this maps to capacity):
  - avg_tokens_per_request = 180
  - steady QPS = 8 rps (approx)
  - peak QPS = 65 rps (15m window)
  - avg_concurrency = 30
  - streaming_required = yes
  - target p95 = 400ms

If you can paste numbers into the attached redwood_throughput_template.csv, I'll run them through our sizing tool and return a recommended config (model variant, #GPUs, autoscale buffer, estimated tokens/sec and expected p95).

I'll also pull a first-pass throughput_estimate_v1.xlsx and a few notes about batching/kv-cache tradeoffs once we have your inputs.

Cheers,
Marissa Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
---
Attachment: redwood_throughput_template.csv (CSV template)

From: Alice Johnson <alice@finex.com>

Cc: Bob Miller <bob.procurement@finex.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex performance targets

Hi Rafael / Marissa

Thanks for the clear checklist. I've filled in the numbers below (also attached a short sample trace):

- avg_tokens_per_request: 210 (avg prompt 150 + expected completion 60)
- requests_per_second_steady: 12
- requests_per_second_peak: 120 (this is a short 10-15m burst during market open)
- avg_concurrency: 90 (many simultaneous chat sessions during peak)
- session_length_requests: 6 (average multi-turn session)
- streaming_required: yes (we stream tokens to the client for an interactive UI)
- desired_latency_slos: p50 ~180ms, p95 <= 400ms for responses under 256 tokens
- context_window: mostly short (<=2048 tokens) with occasional long reports (<=8k)
- cacheable_prefix: yes system prompts and user profile data ~70% reuse

Notes: peak is highly bursty at market open (8:30-8:45 ET), sustained for ~10-15 minutes. Outside that window traffic is fairly steady with diurnal pattern. We can provide a week of trace logs if that helps.

Attaching a small sample trace and an exported QPS chart. Let me know if you need the raw logs.

Best,
Alice Johnson
Head of Product, Conversational AI | Finex, Inc.
alice@finex.com

Perfect, thanks for these numbers very helpful. Marissa, with the inputs below can you run the sizing tool and propose:

  - estimated GPUs and autoscale headroom to hit p95 <= 400ms with streaming enabled
  - expected tokens/sec and QPS capacity per node, and an estimate for a Dedicated pool vs Hosted SLA

Alice: provisional next steps from our side:
  1) Marissa will send throughput_estimate_v1.xlsx with a few config options (shared/dedicated, #GPUs, estimated monthly token volume).
  2) If the Dedicated path looks right, we can schedule a 30-min sizing call Monday to walk the perf numbers and discuss SLA/contracting timeline.
  3) We'll also include notes on KV prefix caching and batching parameters to reduce peak GPU needs given the bursty market-open pattern.

I'll include an initial cost ballpark in the worksheet. If you want the raw logs uploaded to a secure S3 link for analysis, we can accept that happy to have your team drop them into the Drive link I shared.
